concepts.why: Patient has a medical history of infective endocarditis and recently underwent tricuspid valve replacement, with current findings of pulmonic valve vegetations and severe tricuspid valve regurgitation.
Patient recently underwent tricuspid valve replacement and has severe tricuspid valve regurgitation secondary to a flail leaflet.
Patient has heart rates between 150 and 190 beats per minute and a grouped beating pattern with 1 P wave producing 2 QRS complexes.
Patient has a blood pressure of 94/60 mm Hg.
It explains the electrocardiogram finding of P waves upright in leads II, III, and aVF with sinus rate of 96 beats per minute and a regularly irregular rhythm.

rationales.F02: Patient has a medical history of infective endocarditis, which increases the likelihood of current infective endocarditis.
rationales.F04: Recent tricuspid valve replacement is a risk factor for both infective endocarditis and tricuspid valve regurgitation.
rationales.F06: Episodes of light-headedness can be a symptom of tachycardia and hypotension.
rationales.F07: Chest pain can be a symptom of tachycardia and hypotension.
rationales.F08: Low blood pressure is a defining characteristic of hypotension.
rationales.F09: High heart rates are a defining characteristic of tachycardia.
rationales.F10: The electrocardiogram findings suggest a possible atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia.
rationales.F11: The grouped beating pattern with 1 P wave producing 2 QRS complexes is consistent with tachycardia and possibly atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia.
rationales.F12: Pulmonic valve vegetations and severe tricuspid valve regurgitation are indicative of infective endocarditis and tricuspid valve regurgitation.
